Group 1 (Case 1):
Here is the student’s answer for this case:
1. Case 1: Pressure-induced ear necrosis
The patient developed erythematous necrotic ear plaques after prone positioning, with lesions at pressure points. Biopsy showing full-thickness epidermal and dermal necrosis with adnexal necrosis and sparse inflammation is consistent with pressure-induced ischemic necrosis. The absence of septic vasculitis and vascular thrombi/hemorrhage argues against septic embolic and coagulopathic necrosis. Although Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia is present, the histologic findings are atypical for septic emboli, and factor VII deficiency does not support a thrombotic cause. Therefore, pressure-induced ear necrosis is the favored diagnosis and sufficiently explains the clinical picture.
